q: Three 1/0 AWG THHN (0.1855 in² each) and one 2 AWG THHN (0.1158 in²) are installed in EMT. The minimum trade size is:
explain: Total area = 3 × 0.1855 + 0.1158 = 0.6723 in². Table 4 EMT at 40%: 1¼ in. = 0.598 in² (too small), 1½ in. = 0.814 in². Use 1½ in.

q: How many 8 AWG THHN conductors are permitted in ¾-in. EMT?
explain: Table C.1: 8 AWG THHN — ½ in. → 3, ¾ in. → 6, 1 in. → 9.

q: Twelve 10 AWG THHN current-carrying conductors share a raceway in a 40°C ambient. The adjusted and corrected ampacity of each is approximately:
explain: Start at the 90°C column: 40 A. 10–20 conductors → 50%; 36–40°C → 0.91. 40 × 0.50 × 0.91 ≈ 18.2 A — so a 20 A device is the practical maximum, below the 30 A small-conductor cap.

q: A box contains six 14 AWG circuit conductors, two internal cable clamps, one single-pole switch, and three 14 AWG equipment grounding conductors. Minimum box volume?
explain: 6 conductors + 1 (all clamps together) + 2 (device yoke) + 1 (all EGCs together) = 10 volumes × 2.00 in³ = 20 in³.

q: Three 12-2 NM cables (each with a ground) enter a box that holds a switch and a duplex receptacle, with no internal clamps. Minimum box volume?
Two 2-in. conduits enter a pull box on the same wall and the conductors leave through two 2-in. conduits on the same wall (a U-pull). The minimum distance to the opposite wall is:
explain: 6 × 2 in. (largest raceway) + 2 in. (the other raceway in the same row on that wall) = 14 in. The 6× rule also applies between each entry and exit of the same conductor group.

q: Direct-buried conductors emerging from grade must be protected by an enclosure or raceway extending from the minimum cover depth up to at least how far above finished grade?
explain: Protection runs from the required burial depth (or 18 in. below grade) to a point at least 8 ft above finished grade.

q: The 75°C ampacity of 4/0 AWG aluminum is:
Electrical metallic tubing shall NOT be used:
choices: Where subject to severe physical damage
In wet locations with listed fittings
explain: EMT is thin-wall. It is also not permitted for direct earth burial where subject to corrosion unless protected, or to support luminaires except as permitted.

q: Between pull points (boxes, conduit bodies), a run of rigid metal conduit or EMT shall contain not more than the equivalent of how many degrees of bends?
explain: Four quarter bends (360°) total, including offsets, between pull points.

q: The sum of the cross-sectional areas of all conductors in a metal wireway shall not exceed what percentage of its interior area?
explain: Wireways: 20% fill (and adjustment factors apply only above 30 current-carrying conductors, 376.22(B)).

q: Where raceways contain insulated conductors of what minimum size must a fitting or bushing with a smooth insulating surface protect the conductors where they enter an enclosure?
explain: 4 AWG and larger conductors need an insulating bushing or an identified fitting at raceway terminations, unless separated by substantial insulating material.

q: Rigid PVC conduit in trade sizes ½ in. through 1 in. must be supported at intervals not exceeding:
explain: Table 352.30: ½–1 in. → 3 ft; 1¼–2 in. → 5 ft; 2½–3 in. → 6 ft; 3½–5 in. → 7 ft; 6 in. → 8 ft. Also within 3 ft of each termination.
